title: CatBoost evaluates fragility-fracture risk in a community cohort
summary: CatBoost evaluated fragility-fracture risk in 2,227 participants from the Korean Ansung cohort followed for a mean 7.5 years. Reported total-fracture AUC was 0.688, compared with 0.663 for FRAX, using repeated internal cross-validation. The study also ranked candidate predictors, but did not estimate time to fracture or demonstrate benefit from model-guided prevention. External populations remain to be tested.
organization: Seoul National University College of Medicine

source_review.scope: Primary full paper relevant model Methods, study Results and limitations; exact primary front-matter identity and Europe PMC metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Retrospective outcome modeling within a longitudinal cohort, with three-fold cross-validation repeated 1,000 times.
evidence.unknown: External ethnic/population validation, time-to-event prediction and clinical benefit remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Categorical gradient boosting learns fracture-risk relationships from clinical variables and is compared with FRAX, SVM and logistic regression.
